Sleep example: actigraphy SQI read on the PSQI components

Source: vignettes/sleep-simulation.Rmd
sleep-simulation.Rmd

This vignette walks through the worked example of the manuscript: a simulated data set (n = 1000) in which seven PSQI component scores (C1 to C7, 0 to 3) and an actigraphy sleep-quality index (SQI, higher = better sleep) are driven by one latent sleep-disturbance trait. The generating SQI curve is the quadratic 72 − 8η − 1.5η² with residual SD 6; it is used only as the truth.

The light steps below run when the vignette is built. The bootstrap and the simulation study take tens of minutes to hours and are shown, not run; the full analysis scripts are in system.file("scripts", package = "caliber").

Data

The data ship with the package as the data set psqi_sleep (see ?caliber::psqi_sleep). sleep_data() returns it without the true trait, which sleep_eta_true() keeps apart for evaluation.

library(caliber)
dat <- sleep_data()
items <- paste0("C", 1:7)
Y <- as.matrix(dat[items]); sqi <- dat$SQI
summary(dat$PSQI_global); cor(dat$PSQI_global, sqi)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   0.000   4.000   6.000   6.622   9.000  21.000
#> [1] -0.702831

Step 1: the GRM on the PSQI alone 

grm <- fit_grm(Y)
round(cbind(a = grm$a, b = -grm$d / grm$a), 2)
#>         a                
#> [1,] 2.31 -0.84 0.98 2.07
#> [2,] 1.28 -1.00 0.44 1.59
#> [3,] 1.35  0.00 1.07 2.19
#> [4,] 1.92  0.38 1.11 1.80
#> [5,] 1.23 -2.33 0.88 3.16
#> [6,] 0.83  1.44 2.41 2.96
#> [7,] 1.44 -0.95 0.99 2.77

Step 2: the monotone SQI curve, MS-Fixed

MS-Fixed holds the items at the PSQI-only estimates and integrates the latent trait out over p(η | C, SQI) at every boosting iteration. It is the recommended primary analysis; MS-Joint (mode = "joint") is the robustness check and MS-EAP (mode = "eap") the naive comparator. fit_three() fits all three.

fit <- fit_ms(grm, Y, sqi, mode = "fixed")
c(iter = fit$iter, df = round(fit$df, 2), sigma0 = round(fit$act$sigma, 2),
  g1 = round(fit$act$log_sigma[2], 3))
#>    iter      df  sigma0      g1 
#> 1046.00    4.46    5.74   -0.06
round(mu_sqi(-3:3, fit$act), 1)
#> [1] 79.5 79.5 78.3 72.7 62.5 48.7 28.7

Alternative curve: Ramsay’s monotone regression splines

fit_ms(curve = "ispline") replaces the boosting by Ramsay’s (1988) monotone regression splines: μ(η) = β0 − Σ a_m I_m(η) with a_m ≥ 0, I-splines of order 2 on a few interior knots at quantiles of N(0, 1) (median, terciles, …), fitted by maximum likelihood under the bounds. The number of knots is chosen by AIC among 0 to 5. The three ways of handling the latent trait are the same.

fit_i <- fit_ms(grm, Y, sqi, mode = "fixed", curve = "ispline")
fit_i$path[c("n_knots", "deviance", "df", "aic")]
#>   n_knots deviance df      aic
#> 1       0 20969.53  4 20977.53
#> 2       1 20959.55  5 20969.55
#> 3       2 20956.96  6 20968.96
#> 4       3 20955.14  7 20969.14
#> 5       4 20955.04  8 20971.04
#> 6       5 20955.03  9 20973.03
c(n_knots = fit_i$n_knots, sigma0 = round(fit_i$act$sigma, 2),
  g1 = round(fit_i$act$log_sigma[2], 3))
#> n_knots  sigma0      g1 
#>   2.000   5.870  -0.034
round(rbind(boosting = mu_sqi(-3:3, fit$act), ispline = mu_sqi(-3:3, fit_i$act)), 1)
#>          [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7]
#> boosting 79.5 79.5 78.3 72.7 62.5 48.7 28.7
#> ispline  83.3 81.2 77.6 72.3 62.6 49.7 33.8

Step 3: interpretation in SQI units

Each GRM threshold b_jk is placed on the SQI scale at s_jk = μ(b_jk).

thr <- threshold_locations(fit$a, fit$d, fit$act)
dimnames(thr$sqi) <- list(items, paste0("k", 1:3))
round(thr$sqi, 1)
#>      k1   k2   k3
#> C1 77.6 62.7 48.0
#> C2 78.3 67.7 54.8
#> C3 72.7 61.8 47.0
#> C4 68.5 61.3 51.6
#> C5 79.5 63.6 18.9
#> C6 57.0 45.6 31.3
#> C7 78.1 62.6 40.2

The probabilistic crosswalk gives the expected PSQI response pattern at a given SQI, averaging over the latent values compatible with it.

cw <- crosswalk(c(50, 60, 70, 80), fit$a, fit$d, fit$act, items, total_name = "PSQI")
round(cw[c("SQI", "E_PSQI", "Estar_PSQI")], 2)
#>   SQI E_PSQI Estar_PSQI
#> 1  50  13.30      14.39
#> 2  60   9.69      11.30
#> 3  70   6.24       7.04
#> 4  80   4.01         NA
th <- data.frame(item = rep(items, 3), k = rep(1:3, each = 7), sqi_est = c(thr$sqi))
pv <- plausible_values(fit, grm, sqi, seed = 20261004)
wright_map_sqi(mu_sqi(pv, fit$act), th, sleep_item_labels)

Wright map on the SQI scale, MS-Fixed.

Intervals

Item parameters, thresholds within the data and the crosswalk get intervals from draws of the normal approximation of the estimates:

vc <- ms_vcov(fit, Y, sqi)
iv <- ms_intervals(fit, vc, function(a, d, act) {
  s <- threshold_locations(a, d, act)$sqi
  setNames(c(s), paste0("s_", threshold_names(items)))
}, n_draw = 2000, seed = 1)

These draws condition on the selected boosting path and miss most of the sampling variance of the curve itself (SD of μ̂(0) 0.26 against a true 0.61), so curve bands come from the nonparametric bootstrap, which refits every step:

boot <- ms_bootstrap(Y, sqi, n_boot = 200, keep_categories = FALSE, cores = 4)
boot_intervals(boot, "MS-Fixed", paste0("mu(", -3:3, ")"))

Neither kind of interval has been validated by a coverage simulation. The top thresholds of C5, C6 and C7 lie beyond the data and should be reported as beyond data support, not with an interval.

Simulation study

inst/scripts/sleep_simulation.R runs six scenarios × 200 replications (about 3 hours on 4 cores) and sleep_simulation_summary.R makes the tables and figures. One replication:

d <- simulate_scenario(s = 4, r = 1)        # gentle logistic truth
f <- fit_three(d$Y, d$sqi)
tr <- scenario_truth(4, seq(15, 95, by = 0.5))
sqrt(mean((threshold_locations(f$`MS-Fixed`$a, f$`MS-Fixed`$d, f$`MS-Fixed`$act)$sqi - tr$thr)^2))
